context:
User request: A button that plays a 5-second melody in C major at 120 BPM, four notes per bar, built from sine tones computed sample by sample with math.sin at 8000 samples per second, sent as comma-separated 16-bit samples to the platform audio renderer write call with sampleRate 8000. On every beat the flashlight turns on, and it turns off 80 milliseconds later, in time with the melody. When the melody ends, the flashlight is off and the app shows how many beats it blinked.
Widget brief: Local interactive mini-app. Single primary button "Play". On press, synthesize a 5-second melody in C major, 120 BPM, 4 notes per bar (1 beat = 0.5 s, so a 5 s melody = 10 beats = 2.5 bars). Generate audio sample-by-sample with Math.sin at 8000 samples/s (total 40000 samples), and play via the platform audio renderer using the comma-separated 16-bit integer sample string with sampleRate 8000. Use a simple C major scale/arpeggio melody assigned per beat; apply short fade to avoid clicks. On every beat (every 0.5 s from start) turn the flashlight on, then off 80 ms later. When the melody ends, ensure flashlight is off (explicit off call) and display a beat counter showing how many beats the flashlight blinked (10 total). Also show status (idle / playing / finished). Disable Play while playing. Handle flashlight unavailability gracefully with a note that blinking is unavailable, while audio still plays. Interface language: English.
Excerpts below may be truncated. Preserve the complete request, brief, and source URLs above.
Reply excerpt: I'll build a mini-app with that button, the synthesized C major melody, and the flashlight blinking on each beat.
